text:
Hello lovers of the traditional deck, and welcome to the


This contest aims to encourage the creation of games accessible to anyone who has one or more decks of traditional playing cards. The contest was started by Iffix Y. Santaph and it was held in 2021, 2022 and 2023.

 Contest Results

 Contest Geeklist
 Entry list
 Reviews of the games from the contest (by Jenard Cabilao)

Dates
 Earliest Date for Games to be Publicly Available: September 1st, 2024
 Deadline for submissions: December 1st, 2024
 Deadline for mandatory feedback: December 10th, 2024
 Development: Until December 15th, 2024
 Voting: December 15th to December 31st, 2024

Components
The main components of the game should be the cards from the traditional deck of playing cards (the French or poker deck).

If you are using multiple decks, these may have different backs or the same backs, and you may use these mechanically, within reason.

You can also adjust the size of the deck, removing unnecessary cards, though your final game must include and be based on a traditional deck of playing cards. Jokers are fine as well. You can also use a deck box as a component if you can find a mechanical reason to do so.

A small amount of coins, chips, cubes, dice or other common items is permitted. (The harder these items are to come by, the fewer players will play and vote for your game. So weigh out personally whether such components are really necessary.)

No printable custom components are allowed in this contest, with the exception of components that don't have a gameplay function: the rulebook, scorepad, player aids or a reference sheet.

Mechanisms and player count
The game may use any mechanism, new or well-established. But, the game should not be a simple small variant from another common card game.

Any player count is permitted.

Submitting your game

 Create a WIP thread for your game in the Works in Progress forum .
Include the phrase [2024 Traditional Deck Game Design Contest] as well as [IDEA PHASE] or [RULES AVAILABLE] in the thread's title.
The Original Post (OP) should include a link back to this thread.

 You MUST add your game to the contest geeklist.
If the game is not in the geeklist - it's not in the contest!
In the geeklist entry (and in your WIP thread's OP), please include a list of any additional components needed to play your game, as well as player count, earliest age, and estimated length of play.

 Post a link to your WIP thread here in the contest thread, so that others know about your game.

 When the rules become available for your game, post the file link(s) in the top post of your WIP thread and also here. This will alert potential players that they can start to playtest your game.

Each designer or design team may submit at most 2 designs to this contest. Designing as a part of a team is allowable, but each individual designer in the team may submit no more than 2 designs to the contest.

Feedback
For the benefit of all, entrants are required to post feedback on at least three other games for each one that they enter. If you enter a game, you should give meaningful feedback on at least three others. If you enter two games, give feedback on six others. Not only does this benefit both designers, but it also helps to make the voting results meaningful. Keep in mind that the more feedback you are willing to share, usually, the more others will share in return.

You may occasionally use this thread to request feedback for your game or to offer feedback to others who may need it. But all such feedback should be given in the threads of the games individually, and not here. In the event that you or someone else makes a YouTube video of the gameplay they'd like to share, please make mention of that here. In addition, if you are making a feedback video for someone else, please let them know in private message, rather than directly posting into their thread. Allow the designer to share the video if they wish.

These contests are great way to interact with fellow designers, play test their games and in turn let people play your game. Accept both positive and negative feedback graciously, and give useful feedback in turn. You are not just participating in the contest, you are participating in the community.

Other information
The organiser reserves the right to make the final decision on any issues arising from the contest rules.

If you need to withdraw your game, for whatever reason, simply post a note about it here.

At all times all the rights to your game stay with you. Rest assured that this is a very friendly and creative community and nobody is going to steal your ideas.

It's OK to use AI art for illustrations in this contest. Whether you use AI or stock art, or something else, please make note in your OP of the source for the images and the software you used (AI model or graphic design software). This benefits us all as we become aware of the various options to create illustrations to promote our games.

The most important rule is: HAVE FUN!

Now go create some awesome games! 

Note: Some text above was taken from the 2 Player Design Contest organized by John Kean.
The logo for the contest was created in Canva using Canva stock art.

The contest will have two equal winners, one in the Best Solo Game category, and another in the Best Multiplayer Game category. This way the multiplayer games get their spot in the sun, as solo games tend to get more feedback.

Feel free to tip some geekgold to the categories below, it is much appreciated.

The winners in all categories will be determined by voting via Google Forms. The voting part of the contest will be run by the awesome

Voting starts December 15th!

Who can vote, and other questions:


Ben Morayta
@bmorayta1
Q: Who can vote?
Q: Can I vote?
Q: Can I vote if I don't have a game in the contest?
Q: Can I vote if I didn't give feedback, but played the games?
Q: Can I vote if I didn't give feedback, but followed some games' WIPs and their progress?
A: Yes! If you have a BGG account, created before the start of the contest, you can vote.

Q: Can I vote for a game if I didn't play it?
A: Yes! If you have an opinion on a game based on the components, the rulebook, the art, the mechanics described, etc. you can vote for it (although your vote will not be counted the same as a vote from someone that played the game).

Q: Can I vote for my own game?
A: Absolutely, you should! But probably only if you like it...
You can find more answers in the Solitaire PnP Contest FAQ , which applies to this contest as well.
